hypothesis: Whisper's hallucinated closing phrases (terima kasih / sampai jumpa) sit at clip ends and cost insertions, so stripping them should lower WER
conclusion: tail beats diacritics-only 0.1760 -> 0.1744: I 51->45, S 497->495, D 78->80, net 626->620 errors; same direction and size as the v2 sweep, and the mechanism (hallucinated closing phrases) is model-side, not annotator convention.

hypothesis: a leading hallucinated 'hai' greeting is the same failure mode as the tail and should remove one more insertion
conclusion: hai is a no-op on v5 convo-2 output: byte-identical metrics to p003 (0.1744, 495/80/45); the tuned model never opens a clip with a hallucinated greeting, so the rule costs nothing and adds nothing.

hypothesis: VAD filtering should suppress the hallucinated speech Whisper invents over non-speech regions, cutting insertions at the source rather than by a postproc rule
conclusion: VAD hurts: 0.1774 vs 0.1760. It does cut deletions (78->74) but adds 11 substitutions (497->508) by clipping speech at segment edges; net errors 626->631. Reject; the tail postproc rule is the better handle on hallucinated audio.

hypothesis: a wider beam explores more of the lexical-variant space that dominates the remaining substitutions, so beam 8 may pick references' variant more often than beam 5
conclusion: beam 8 ties beam 5 (0.1769 vs 0.1760, 629 vs 626 errors) at 60% more decode time, reproducing the v2 sweep on v5; beam 5 stays. Wider search does not resolve the lexical-variant substitutions.

hypothesis: if the tail gain is a real failure mode and not one lucky clip it should reproduce on the beam-8 decode too
conclusion: tail reproduces independently: on the beam-8 decode it gives 0.1769 -> 0.1746 (I 52->44), same direction and magnitude as p003 on beam 5, so the gain is a real hallucinated-tail failure mode rather than one lucky clip.

hypothesis: turbo spends 192 of 232 LoRA modules on its 32-layer encoder, adapted mostly on 8 h of clean read TTS Javanese whose acoustics do not match noisy dev conversation; a decoder-only adapter should keep the Javanese lexical transfer without dragging the encoder toward read-speech audio
conclusion: Coarse screen only: decoder-only on the v5 mix is no gross regression (0.1783 at 500 chunks / 1 epoch, in range of every other proxy) and trains 2x faster (267s vs ~545s) on 4.3M params vs 27.9M. There is no all-scope proxy on this same mix, so this number ranks nothing; it clears the change for a full run. Composition shift worth watching: D 106 vs 66-69 elsewhere, I 38, i.e. the low-capacity adapter is still closer to base Whisper's deletion-heavy behaviour after 1 epoch.

hypothesis: turbo puts 192 of its 232 LoRA-targeted modules in the 32-layer encoder, which the v5 mix adapts mostly on 8 h of clean read TTS audio that does not match noisy dev conversation; restricting LoRA to the 4-layer decoder should keep the Javanese lexical transfer while leaving the acoustic encoder at its base-model robustness
conclusion: Decoder-only LoRA on the v5 mix scores 0.1707 vs v5's 0.1760 (-0.0053; ind 0.1359->0.1243, javind 0.1889->0.1855, errors 626->607) and its in-training val agrees independently: best epoch 0.1710 vs v5's 0.1798, with the same 3-epoch schedule and ep3 regressing in both. 4.3M trainable params vs 27.9M and 25 min wall vs ~100. Treat the margin as unconfirmed until full-run noise is measured.

hypothesis: the hallucinated-tail gain measured on two v5 decodes should carry to the decoder-only model's output
conclusion: tail carries to the decoder-only model: 0.1707 -> 0.1699 (I 44->40), the third independent decode where it helps; first sub-0.17 number in the project.

hypothesis: replication: if decoder-only LoRA is genuinely better than the all-scope v5 mix and not a lucky run, an independent seed should land near 0.1707 again rather than back at v5's 0.1760
conclusion: Replication, seed 1: 0.1738 (early-stopped after 2 epochs, best 0.1758 in-training). Decoder-only now has two independent runs at 0.1707 and 0.1738, mean 0.1723, spread 0.0031 - both under v5's 0.1760 but by roughly the size of the spread, so the margin is real in direction and unproven in size. First measurement of full-run seed variance in this project.

hypothesis: if decoder-only wins by sparing the encoder rather than by having fewer parameters, giving the decoder adapter more capacity at rank 64 should hold or improve on rank 32; if it wins by regularisation, rank 64 should give the gain back
conclusion: Rank 64 decoder-only scores 0.1693, the best full run so far (ind 0.1185, the best Indonesian number in the project; javind 0.1855). More decoder capacity does not give the gain back, so decoder-only wins by sparing the encoder from 8 h of clean read TTS audio, not by having fewer parameters. Three decoder-only runs now sit at 0.1693/0.1707/0.1738, all below v5's 0.1760.

hypothesis: the r32->r64 improvement says decoder capacity is still binding, so rank 128 should continue the curve; a turn upward would locate the capacity ceiling for a 4-layer decoder on 9.8 h
conclusion: Rank 128 decoder-only scores 0.1670 (ind 0.1127, javind 0.1844), best full run in the project. The decoder-only capacity curve is monotone at seed 0: r32 0.1707, r64 0.1693, r128 0.1670, and the gain is concentrated on the Indonesian side (ind 0.1359 -> 0.1127, about -20 errors on 861 words) while javind moves only 0.1889 -> 0.1844, so the headline number leans on 20 of the 78 clips.

hypothesis: combine the two independent wins: hallucinated-tail stripping on the rank-128 decoder-only model
conclusion: tail is a no-op on the rank-128 decoder-only model: metrics byte-identical at 0.1670, 478/69/47. The stronger decoder adaptation has already removed the hallucinated closing phrases the rule was patching, so the postproc win and the training win are not additive - they fix the same errors.

hypothesis: replication of the best configuration: an independent seed should reproduce rank-128 decoder-only near 0.1670 if the capacity curve is real rather than three draws of run-to-run noise
conclusion: Rank 128 at seed 1 gives 0.1707, not 0.1670: the rank effect (0.0037 across r32->r128 at seed 0) is the same size as the seed spread (0.0031 at r32, 0.0037 at r128), so the capacity curve is NOT separable from run-to-run noise and rank 128 must not be called better than rank 32. What survives: all five decoder-only runs (0.1670/0.1693/0.1707/0.1707/0.1738, mean 0.1703) sit at or below v5's single 0.1760.

hypothesis: control: reproduce the v5 mix with the historical all-scope LoRA under the runner, to test whether the decoder-only advantage survives once the baseline is measured on the same pipeline rather than quoted from one older run
conclusion: CONTROL, and it reframes the night: retraining v5's exact recipe (all-scope r32, same mix, same flags) today scores 0.1718, not the 0.1760 on record from 2026-09-23. The historical number does not reproduce in the current environment; in-training ep1 is 0.1773 today vs 0.2166 then. Decoding the frozen runs/ct2/lora_v5 weights still gives 0.1760 (d001), so the drift is in training, not scoring. Measured against this same-day control instead of the quoted 0.1760, decoder-only r32 (mean 0.1723) is a wash and r128 (mean 0.1689) leads by only 0.0029, inside the seed spread.

hypothesis: second all-scope point: the decoder-only comparison rests on a single same-day control, so measuring the baseline's own seed spread decides whether the remaining 0.0029 gap at rank 128 means anything
conclusion: All-scope seed 1 scores 0.1676, better than its own seed 0 (0.1718) and better than four of the five decoder-only runs. Baseline seed spread is 0.0042, larger than decoder-only's 0.0031-0.0037. Arm means: all-scope 0.1697 (n=2), decoder-only r32 0.1723 (n=2), r128 0.1689 (n=2) - all inside each other's noise. The decoder-only accuracy hypothesis is NOT confirmed; what survives is equal accuracy at 2-3x the training speed and ~6x fewer trainable parameters. javind 0.1785 here is the best Javanese number of the night while its ind 0.1336 is worse than the decoder-only runs, so even the language split shuffles with seed.

hypothesis: third baseline seed: the all-scope arm shows the largest spread of the night (0.1676-0.1718), so a third point is what decides whether the decoder-only arm differs from it at all
conclusion: All-scope seed 2 scores 0.1670, exactly tying t016, the best decoder-only run of the night. All-scope now has three points: 0.1718 / 0.1676 / 0.1670, mean 0.1688, sd 0.0027. Decoder-only r128 mean is 0.1689 over two points. The two arms are indistinguishable on accuracy, which retires the decoder-only accuracy hypothesis and leaves its 2-3x speed and 6x parameter reduction as the only real difference.

hypothesis: third decoder-only r128 seed to make the comparison a symmetric 3-vs-3: with the all-scope arm at mean 0.1688 (sd 0.0027) the decoder-only arm needs a matching third point before either can be called equal or different
conclusion: Decoder-only r128 seed 2 scores 0.1715, completing a symmetric 3-vs-3. All-scope r32: 0.1718/0.1676/0.1670, mean 0.1688, sd 0.0027. Decoder-only r128: 0.1670/0.1707/0.1715, mean 0.1697, sd 0.0024. The difference is 0.0009 in favour of all-scope, about a third of one standard deviation - the two are indistinguishable on accuracy. Decoder-only's real advantage is cost: 1499s vs 4922s per full run and 6.5x fewer trainable parameters at r32.
